title: Austin Considers Major Gas Contract
summary:
*   The Austin City Council held a special meeting solely to discuss a proposed new gas contract for the city.
*   They heard detailed presentations, including a geological report from consultants, and received input from an appointed advisory committee.
*   After a long discussion, the Council decided to further study a proposed letter of intent for the contract, seeking additional input and potential amendments from the advisory committee before making a final commitment.

Special Meeting
July 21, 1958
11:00 Α.Μ.
Council Chamber, City Hall
The meeting was called to order with Mayor Miller presiding. Roll call: Present:
Councilmen Long, Palmer, Pearson, White, Mayor Miller Absent:
None
Present also: W. T. Williams, Jr., City Manager; Doren R. Eskew, City Attorney; D. K.
Kinney, Director of Electric Utilities.
The Mayor announced that this was a meeting called to discuss a proposed gas contract.
Present were MR. E. W. JACKSON, MR. TED WIMBERLY, and MR. JAMES NASH, members of an
Advisory Committee appointed by the Council.
MR. JOHN PUNDT gave a resume of the developments of his progress up to this time, and
asked that the City write a letter of acceptance so that they could proceed. MR. BUCK WINN
went into details about the progress. MR.
BRINKERHOFF, Consultant, made a geological report.
After a long discussion, the Council took under study a proposed letter stating that the
City was prepared to execute a contract in keeping with the letter of intent, subject to
certain provisions. The Mayor stated the Council wanted to go over this more, and ask the
advisory committee to study the letter and maybe make some amendments or some suggestions.
There being no further business, the Council adjourned at 2:30 P.M., subject to the call
of the Mayor.
